body.x: FIX 2026 (Future Innovation Tech Expo), South Korea’s benchmark future industry exhibition marking its third edition this year, will be held from Wednesday, October 21 to Saturday, October 24 at EXCO in Daegu. Under the slogan “AI, Beyond Tech into Reality,” the expo establishes a new standard for global industry by integrating and linking technologies and services across four key new sectors: future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. Showcasing the fruits of Daegu Metropolitan City’s initiatives to foster advanced future industries, this stage will gather global tech unicorns and innovative startups to unveil blueprints for next-generation industries. Concurrently featuring international conferences, global business matchmaking sessions, and open innovation programs, the event is set to serve as a pivotal hub for exchange, driving technological innovation far beyond South Korea.

Participating as an official Global Media Award partner for FIX 2026, DIGITIMES is a global technology media outlet and research institute specializing in IT and electronics supply chain analysis. By delivering in-depth insights into global high-tech manufacturing ecosystems—encompassing semiconductors, AI hardware infrastructure, mobility, and displays—DIGITIMES has earned authoritative credibility among C-level executives and industry professionals worldwide. With extensive networks connected to global manufacturing and foundry clusters, DIGITIMES has consistently tracked value chain connectivity with South Korea’s core tech enterprises. Beyond reporting on standalone technical specifications, DIGITIMES provides differentiated supply chain perspectives that examine industrial positioning and commercial scalability, serving as a strategic bridge again this year between promising Korean tech enterprises and a worldwide readership. A pre-event interview was conducted with reporter Sherri Wang, who is covering FIX 2026 following her coverage of FIX 2025, to hear her perspectives on this year’s exhibition.

body.cap: A screenshot from Digitime's main page

body.x: 1. Could you please introduce your media to a Korean audience?

DIGITIMES is a technology news and research organization focused on the global tech supply chain. We cover semiconductors, AI infrastructure, ICT, electric vehicles, displays and other emerging technologies, combining daily reporting with industry research and analysis.

For Korean companies, I think what sets DIGITIMES apart is our supply-chain perspective. Our readers want to know not just what a new technology does, but where a company fits in the global ecosystem, who its potential customers and partners are, whether the technology can scale, and how competitive it could be internationally.
2. What do you think about recent trends in industrial technology, mobility, and AI?

One of the biggest shifts I see is the growing convergence of AI with physical industries. The conversation is moving beyond generative AI and large language models toward physical AI — how AI can interact with robots, vehicles, machines, and real-world industrial environments.

South Korea is especially interesting in this transition. According to the International Federation of Robotics, it has the world’s highest robot density in manufacturing, with 1,220 industrial robots per 10,000 manufacturing employees. Its electronics and automotive industries are major drivers of that demand.
A key question now is how South Korea builds on that strong automation base and strengthens the broader robotics value chain, from core components and software to AI and systems integration.

More broadly, I think the next phase of competition will be about integration — bringing together AI, semiconductors, robotics, mobility, sensors, components, and software to turn them into commercially viable products and services. For journalists covering technology and global supply chains, that is one of the most important developments to watch.

body.cap: HL Robotics’ demonstration of its autonomous parking robots at its booth at FIX 2025 | Photo by Digitimes

body.x: 3. What major issues and topics related to FIX 2026 are your media’s audience most interested in?
Our readers are especially interested in AI infrastructure, semiconductors, robotics and physical AI, next-generation mobility, and the supply chains behind those technologies.

At FIX 2026, one of the main things I will be watching is how technologies move from demonstration to real-world deployment. A humanoid robot can attract a lot of attention on the show floor, but our readers also want to know whether it has real customers, where it can be deployed, what components and AI technologies are behind it, whether production can scale, and whether there is an international market for it.

The same applies to mobility and AI. We are interested not only in finished products but also in the companies that build the underlying technologies. For Korean companies in particular, I will be looking for technologies that could become part of global supply chains and find markets beyond Korea.
4. How was FIX the last time you participated in 2025, and what do you expect from this year’s edition?

What stood out to me at FIX 2025 was the range of technologies gathered in one place. I could see developments in robotics, AI, mobility and ICT side by side, rather than treating each sector separately.

Robotics was one of the highlights for me. I saw humanoid robots, service and healthcare robots, industrial automation and autonomous parking technology, and I spoke with Korean companies about how they were moving those technologies toward real-world applications. HL Robotics’ autonomous parking robot PARKIE was one example that stood out.
The range of humanoid robots on display also showed how companies are starting to look beyond demonstrations and focus more on practical applications.

That is one of the things I am most interested in seeing this year: how the companies and technologies we saw in 2025 have progressed. Have they won new customers or partnerships? Have they expanded overseas or developed new applications? How much closer are emerging technologies to broader commercial deployment?
I am also looking forward to seeing what new companies emerge this year, particularly in physical AI and robotics.

body.cap: A scene from AeiROBOT’s booth at FIX 2025 | Photo by Digitimes

body.x: 5. What do you think about your media being an official Global Media Award partner? What did you think of the press conference for the FIX Innovation Awards, featuring presentations by exhibitors selected as honorees or Best of FIX winners last year?

Being part of the FIX Global Media Awards gave me a different perspective from simply covering the show as a reporter. As one of the international media judges in 2025, I looked not only at technological innovation, but also at whether a technology was practical, where it could be used, and whether it had the potential to expand across industries and international markets.

I ultimately selected SPG, Young Hyun Robotics, and Robocare. They represented very different parts of the robotics ecosystem, but what stood out to me was that each had a clear real-world use case and potential beyond a single market.

I also found the FIX Innovation Awards press conference useful because it gave international journalists a chance to hear directly from selected companies and ask more detailed questions. At a large trade show, it can be difficult to identify the most interesting companies among hundreds of exhibitors. Bringing a smaller group together made it easier to understand their technologies and decide which stories might matter to an international audience.

For DIGITIMES, I think the value of being a Global Media Award partner lies in its ability to connect promising Korean technology companies with readers and industries outside Korea. The point is not just to give out an award, but to identify technologies with real potential and help international audiences understand why they matter.

body.x: Meanwhile, ten prominent global media partners spanning Europe, the Americas, and Asia are participating as official press partners for FIX 2026, deploying on-site reporting delegations.

The international press corps includes leading technology and industry media representing their respective regions: Le Café du Geek, a French IT, lifestyle, and global tech publication; Clipset, a pioneering Spanish mobile and consumer tech outlet; Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley-based American consumer electronics and innovative tech portal; AVING USA, an American global tech, business, and exhibition media outlet; Otaku Soken, a Japanese subculture and AI, VR, and IT convergence publication; DIGITIMES, world-renowned semiconductor and ICT supply chain media and research agency; VietnamPlus, a state-run multinational comprehensive news portal in Vietnam; ChinaByte, China’s first enterprise digital transformation (DX), IT, and AI publication; ET Manufacturing, an Indian smart factory, robotics, and manufacturing engineering media outlet; and Pokde.net, a Malaysian hardware, gaming, and mobile tech publication.

These global media partners will participate directly in on-site evaluations during the event, including the FIX Innovation Awards press conference and the Global Media Selected Best of FIX 2026 Media Awards, reporting from the front lines of technological developments by innovative enterprises shaping the future of South Korea’s high-tech landscape.
